title: Impact of Increase in Paternity Leave on Employability, Productivity and Family Relationships of Employees
what_it_is: Impact of Increase in Paternity Leave on Employability, Productivity and Family Relationships of Employees

sections.label: Paternity and parental leave provisions
sections.summary: It states 2017 changes making the second week of Paternity Leave mandatory and raising Shared Parental Leave from one to four weeks, and that work with tripartite partners on parental leave will continue.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In 2017, we made the second week of Paternity Leave mandatory and increased Shared Parental Leave from one to four weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Fathers can now take up to eight weeks of leave in total in their child's first year, to bond with their newborns and care for their wives.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: A more sustainable approach is for companies to develop a family-friendly culture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We are heartened that some companies in Singapore are leaning forward to offer additional paternity leave, on top of legislated provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: There are also other ways to provide more flexible leave options for staff; many companies have signed up to the Tripartite Standards on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: As the needs of companies vary, employers, in partnership with their employees, are best placed to assess and implement the family-friendly arrangements suited to the company's context.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: We will continue to work with tripartite partners to review the scope for more parental leave provisions and build a Singapore that is Made For Families.

sections.label: Reviewing parental leave provisions
sections.summary: It states that work with the tripartite partners to review the scope for more parental leave provisions will continue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As I had indicated at COS and earlier, we will continue to work with the tripartite partners to review the scope for more parental leave provisions.

sections.label: Take-up rates by year
sections.summary: It gives take-up rates of 47% in 2016, 53% in 2017, 53% in 2018 and 55% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For example, in 2016, the take-up rate was 47%; in 2017, it was 53%; in 2018, it was 53%; in 2019, it was 55%.

sections.label: Assurance to Mr Louis Ng
sections.summary: It states that Mr Louis Ng can be reassured that this is an area of work that will continue to be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng can be reassured that this is an area of work we will continue to look at.
